title: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

sense.text:
“One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.” The things of old are back today. The same spirits that were back then are back here today. The same morality that was with the righteous back then is back today with the righteous, and the immorality of the immoral is back here as well.

King Solomon is making a comparison. He is not only speaking of the things of heaven that God created. It pertains to men, to the spirits of men.

The sun “hasteth to his place where he arose”, the wind “returneth again according to his circuits”, and the rivers go back to “the place from whence the rivers come”. Everything God made comes back around, and so do the spirits of men.

“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”: meaning spirits, men. “And there is no new thing under the sun.” The same hatred, envy and strife going on today among the brothers is the same thing that was back then.

Many of us are baffled by the things we see on social media, but we should not be. It only lets you know that this Bible is a real book and that you are in the right place.

precepts.why:
For Paul to say what he said here, he had to understand the writings of King Solomon and what Solomon expounded in the first chapter of Ecclesiastes.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime”: the things of our forefathers, the works they displayed and the faith they displayed, both the faithful and those without faith, “were written for our learning.” Why? Because there is no new thing under the sun. What took place in the time of Babylon, in the time of King Solomon and in the Assyrian captivity took place again in the Roman captivity. The same spirits that were back then existed when Paul was present, and so it is for us today.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Many times we are uncomfortable because of trials, tribulations and the things we see occurring, but the word of God is to give us comfort if we read, study and apply. That is only for the believers. If you are moving in unbelief, you will be extremely uncomfortable when trials and tribulations arise.

sense.text:
When the Most High raises up prophets, a new servant or a clearer revelation of truth, corrupt leaders often recognize that their influence is fading. Instead of humbling themselves and submitting to God, they become envious and defensive, and that envy and defense often leads to violence. They try to preserve their position by persecuting the very people God has chosen, verbally and sometimes physically, thinking the persecution may delay God’s purpose. At the end of the day they cannot stop it. They cannot stop the movement.

The Most High put a special spirit on our bishops to be the pioneers of this movement in today’s time. That is something you will just have to accept, and play a role, because we are all looking for the same goal, the kingdom. Nowhere in the scriptures is there an award for getting there first.

So where does the envy and hatred come from? “For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die.” The things of the flesh: jealousy, a major one; lust for money; lust for power. Many of our forefathers battled that lust for power. Some were able to overcome that demon and some succumbed to it. These things happened thousands of years ago, but they were written aforetime for our learning, left as an example for us of what not to be.

“But if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body”: mortify all the things we lust after, whether money, power, sex, anything. Anything contrary to God’s laws is the lust of the flesh. “Ye shall live”: that is eternal life.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God”: that is the charitable good works, the fruits of the spirit. “They are the sons of God.” The brothers are the sons of God, but we have to walk in the spirit and run from the flesh.

A lot of these camps have not been walking in the spirit. They have been walking in the flesh and running from the spirit. So when our light, which is the keeping of the commandments and our good works, shines on their darkness, which is the walking in the flesh, envy and hatred come. That is the agony of defeat: coming to the realization that you are a no good nothing and the Most High is going to put out your candle.

precepts.why:
A good example of living after the flesh were the Pharisees. “Ye are of your father the devil”: that is what you don’t want to be, walking after your father the devil, Satan himself. “And the lusts of your father ye will do”: the lust, the envy, the hatred, the malice, the guile, all the works of the flesh the devil puts on display.

This is self-examination time, even for the brothers and sisters within Israel United in Christ. Are you walking after the lust of your father the devil, or after the fruits of the spirit with Christ? Each one of us has to ask that, and we pray the congregations outside of IUIC ask themselves the same thing.

Christ spoke this to the Pharisees because some of them were moved by an evil spirit: envy, pride, fear, hatred, spiritual blindness, that satanic influence. They were raised in the law, so they knew about Christ, because Christ is in the Old Testament; he came in the volume of the book. When Christ walked on the scene there was no New Testament written yet. So what would possess a doctor of the law, a man well learned in the Old Testament, to kick against the pricks like that, except hatred? There is nothing else.

sense.text:
The Pharisees were afraid that Christ was going to replace them and take their followers, because in the mind of the carnal, those who walk after the flesh, followers equal money. It is just like the Christian church, and no different with some of these camps: they added a little Israelite twist to their doctrine and profess themselves Israelites, but in their mind they are looking after power and money. When members wake up and leave, saying something’s wrong, all this man speaks about 24/7 is the bishop and these men in purple, surely I’m in the wrong place, they watch those dollar bills slowly disappearing and they can’t stand it. It is the same thing as the Pharisees.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council”: that is the Sanhedrin. Whenever you see council or committee pertaining to the Pharisees, it is speaking of the Sanhedrin, an organization of counselors of Pharisees and so forth. “For this man doeth many miracles”: that man being Christ, and his followers.

“If we let him thus alone”: if we leave Christ alone, “all men will believe on him.” The same thing of yesterday is the same thing we see today. If we leave these brothers alone, surely they will heap righteous followers to themselves. So let’s taint them, call them names, slander them, roll up on them on camp and antagonize them, try to get them into a physical confrontation so we can sue them or show the whole world they ain’t righteous, they fighting just like us. That is not going to happen, because God is in charge of this movement, not man.

“And the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” That is what the Pharisees feared.

precepts.why:
Not all the Pharisees feared Christ. “There rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed”: certain of the Pharisees rose up and believed on Christ, “saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” That is the great dispute of Acts 15 over circumcision and the law of Moses; read the whole chapter when you get a chance.

It is brought up because in many of these hateful congregations there are people who see the evil, who might secretly be watching us and just buying time until they also walk out of those doors, because they realize the leaders and the men set up over them are good for nothing. A waste of air, a waste of life, a waste of sperm. Good for nothing: that is what God calls them.

Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a follower of Christ: “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: The same came to Jesus by night.” Why did he come to Jesus by night? It was a secret. He was a secret follower, but he believed on Christ.

Here is another follower of Christ, Joseph of Arimathea. The scriptures don’t mention him being a Pharisee explicitly, but because of his status he was part of many of their councils. “There was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;)”. Not every man was allowed into that council, the council of the Pharisees, the Sanhedrin. This lets you know that Joseph of Arimathea had close relations with the Pharisees, yet he was a follower of Christ.

He “also himself waited for the kingdom of God.” He knew the kingdom of God would only come by the Messiah, Jesus the Christ, and he accepted that. That is why he asked Pilate for the body of Christ: he was a secret follower of Christ.

Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus had the know-how and the testicular fortitude to go against the grain, the grain being the evil movement the Pharisees had to destroy Christ and his followers. These are just the two that are mentioned; surely there were others, for the Bible is written in an abbreviated form. They had the courage to stand up against their leaders and say, No, what y’all doing is wrong, y’all persecuting these brothers wrongfully, the envy and the hatred y’all have is wrong. We pray that same spirit falls on many of these Israelites out there.

Some will stand up, speak out against their wicked leaders, and have the balls to do something about it. But most of the time they stay silent, and silence means you accept it. You agree with it.

sense.text:
“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers.” You want to know why you wicked as hell? Because your leaders wicked as hell. You want to know why you can’t break down the scriptures precept upon precept, and give dumb, stupid, idiotic, moronic breakdowns like John the Baptist was evil and turned against Christ? Because your wicked leaders don’t teach. They are not keeping the scriptures, so their mind has become spiritually black: void of judgment, void of discernment, void of truth. They don’t understand the Bible.

That spirit spreads like osmosis through all the officers and soldiers in the camp. You utter the same rhetoric as your leader, and you can’t break down the scriptures, just like your leader. You go online and say Wormwood is vermouth, or gin or tonic, gin and juice in the water, Hennessy cognac in the water. Dumb, stupid breakdowns, because you are not moving in the spirit. You are moving in the flesh.

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” The fear of the Lord is not breaking his Sabbath, not buying and selling willfully on his Sabbath, not taking trips to 7-Eleven on the Sabbath; it is keeping his commandments.

“A good understanding have all they that do his commandments.” The Most High will elevate your understanding of the scripture, but that only comes with the application of God’s laws. God promised to raise the waters to the kneecap, to the thigh, to the chest, causing your learning and understanding of the scriptures to increase. But when you are not walking in the spirit and not keeping the commandments of God, that water stays stuck at the ankles and will never rise above the soles of your feet. You will never grow as a person.

So leaders who do not keep the commandments have no understanding to give, and their officers come out just like them.

Brothers and sisters, examine yourselves and make sure we don’t fall under this too, because these same spirits are in IUIC. That is why every couple of years there is a shaking of the tree. We had it in 2018 and we recently had it. Every couple of years the Most High is going to shake the tree, and the murmurers and the gossipers will fall.

“These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts”: the lust for power and the envy spoken of earlier. “And their mouth speaketh great swelling words”: words full of vain glory and pride.

“Having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.” That is why they lack the fortitude to say, Hey, what this man is teaching is wrong, when their leader is constantly calling names and slandering. They have other persons in admiration because they want to move up. The congregation has 20 people in it, but they want to be called a captain of a thousand. So they reason: if I follow this wicked leader and murmur and repeat what he does, I’ll move up in rank; so I won’t check him, I’ll flow with him. Because of advantage. So are his officers.

This is a question the Most High is asking: “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” You want to understand doctrine, brothers and sisters? “Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.”

The milk is the sincere understanding of the word, which is God’s laws. God’s laws are what enable us to grow. You don’t give a baby filet mignon and steak; you give a baby milk, to nurture him. It is the same in this truth: God’s laws are what nurture us and cause us to grow.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” Law upon law. To get a good understanding of the Sabbath you go to Leviticus, to Exodus, to Nehemiah, to understand the rules of not breaking God’s Sabbath, not leaning on your own understanding. Here a little in the Old Testament, there a little in the New Testament. That is how you understand the scriptures, and that is what wicked leaders do not teach.

sense.text:
Obsolescence describes something that is passing out of use because something greater, newer or more effective has replaced it: the state of being old-fashioned and no longer useful, even if it still be in good working order. We are all headed toward the kingdom, and the Most High is going to use you. But it is up to you what you want to be used for, good or evil.

“In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old”: the first, old covenant of animal sacrifice, which became obsolete. “Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away”: ready upon Christ’s crucifixion. He did away with the old covenant because he was the lamb of God, the ultimate sacrifice for the nation of Israel, bringing in the new covenant. So the old covenant became obsolete.

The problem is not merely that something old is being replaced. The problem comes when people refuse to accept that God is moving forward. That is when the agony of defeat comes in: you can’t understand or accept what God is doing, or that God is using a particular person, people or organization for a greater purpose because they are more effective. God doesn’t want the old. He wants to use the new, and you won’t accept that.

People like to say that John the Baptist was evil, that he started his own camp and went against Christ. That is complete malarkey, complete BS. This is the righteous response: what a righteous person accepts when they understand that something greater is coming, or that God is using a particular person or organization that has been more effective with the same goal, raising up the elect of God so we can inherit the kingdom and bring this man’s kingdom, Babylon the great, the great Satan, to an end. We all have to have that same mind. When you are moved with envy, hatred and vain glory, you will not accept it.

“Behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him”: the man you baptized in Jordan is teaching the people, and all men are going to him.

“A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven.” So why is it hard for these other camps and organizations to accept that the great work that started from a mustard seed out of a man’s living room in the year 2003 has grown to be this great tree with many branches, and it ain’t done yet? Because of envy and hatred.

But John the Baptist, the same man they say was not in the truth, accepted it. Was John the Baptist in the truth? Absolutely. The question is, are you in the truth?

“I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him.” He understood that he was sent before him. That is why Isaiah prophesied of the voice in the wilderness making the path for something greater than himself.

We are all ambassadors of Christ, laying down the line and setting up the way for Christ when he invades this earth with his troops. Every congregation, every Israelite organization, is supposed to have that same mindset: ambassadors of Christ, not tearing at the arm and foaming at the mouth, fighting and slandering each other.

The bridegroom is Christ. “This my joy therefore is fulfilled”: John came to fulfill his role, because he knew something greater was coming to carry it on. His mission did not become obsolete, but it would decrease.

“He must increase”: Christ must increase, “but I must decrease.” John the Baptist said a lot right here.

The unrighteous response is the works of the flesh: the envy, the fear of losing influence, the accusation, the slander, the violence, murder and anger. That was the response of the Pharisees to Christ, completely contrary to the response of John the Baptist.

Remember what Paul said: the things written aforetime were written for our learning. “Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” He was not supposed to bring the fruit of the ground; he was supposed to bring the firstlings of the flock.
“The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering.” Why? Because Abel did what the Lord said.

“And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” Why was he wroth? He understood the law. He understood what God wanted, and he knew his gift would not be pleasing to the Lord. He was upset because of Abel. Abel shined a light on his darkness. Abel was the righteous one who brought forth what the Lord wanted, and that put a magnifying glass on Cain’s BS.

It is the same today. Our light puts a magnifying glass on a lot of these false doctrines and these Black Hebrew Israelites that won’t get right.

All Cain had to do was check himself and offer the right offering unto the Lord, but he allowed that spirit to dominate. The same in this time: instead of correcting your doctrine and doing the work, walking in the lot God put you in, you make it a competition out of envy and strife. Not to glorify and magnify Christ’s name as an ambassador of Christ on this earth, but for competition. You want to be the HNIC. And now your darkness is being exposed by our light.

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” We know the consequences of bad acts, the consequences of sin. Why get mad? Might as well be honest: I wanted to fulfill the lust of the flesh, to satisfy myself in that moment. So the Most High asks him, “why is thy countenance fallen?”

“Sin lieth at the door”: Satan. “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him”: sin is going to rule over you; Satan is going to rule over you.

“And Cain talked with Abel his brother.” In the process of time, what was going on in those conversations? Abel was teaching, trying to correct his brother. But Cain allowed that anger, that wrath, to accumulate and increase, and the anger became murder: “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He murdered him because he did not check that spirit; he let it dominate him.

We see it all throughout the scriptures. When Saul tried to kill King David, that was hatred inside that manifested and became actions. The Pharisees the same: the anger, the hatred and the envy manifested and became murder. It is going to be the same today. Do not be shocked. We see the buildup.

precepts.why:
“That we should love one another. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” The things written aforetime were written for our learning: John is writing all the way in the time of Rome, thousands of years later, and he is still going back to what happened with Cain.

“Who was of that wicked one”: the child of Satan, the child of the devil. He didn’t check his anger, so he slew his brother. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

Brothers know if their works are evil. You know if your doctrine is garbage. But because of gain, because of money, because of lust, you will preach things contrary to the Bible to fulfill your lust, knowing deep down that what you are doing is wrong.

So Cain didn’t kill Abel because Abel harmed him. Cain killed Abel because Abel’s righteousness revealed Cain’s sin, his disobedience. As Paul said, the things written aforetime were written for our learning, and that pattern of disobedience recurs all throughout the scriptures.

“This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world.” The light is Christ, and also the keeping of the commandments. “And men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil”: that is what we see today.

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” That is Cain hating Abel, and the same hatred today of those whose light exposes their deeds.

“But he that doeth truth”, the keeping of the commandments, “cometh to the light”, comes to Christ and to the keeping of the commandments, “that his deeds may be made manifest”: those are the fruits of the spirit, “that they are wrought in God.”

sense.text: John went back to Cain; now more history, our brother Joseph. “Israel loved Joseph more than all his children”, and when his brethren saw it, “they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.” That hatred started because they saw the affinity Jacob had for Joseph.

“They hated him yet the more”, and again “they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.” The hatred multiplied after every event, multiplying and multiplying. They didn’t see that the spirit of the most high God was working in Joseph.
“And his brethren envied him.” To envy is to covet something. What did they envy Joseph for? His gifts. The dream.
